Automated Model Briefing

⚠ AI-generated text — may be wrong, incomplete, or overconfident. This is automated commentary on experimental model output, not flight advice and not a weather forecast. It has not been reviewed by a meteorologist.

Overall Assessment — Sunday is dry and mostly clear with moderate thermals from about 10–11am, but a strong southwest flow aloft dominates the day. Wind at ridge height runs 30–50+ miles per hour (mph) at the exposed launches and strengthens through the afternoon ahead of Sunday night's storm. Only the lower, more sheltered sites, McClellan and Daydreams, offer a short, careful midday window; the high launches and wrong-facing sites are not flyable.

Site Breakdown

No site rated favorable today.

Not recommended today (9) — click a row for details

McClellan Marginal — Best thermal site of the day with launch-aligned, moderate wind, but thermals are sharp and the wind above launch is strong.
Window: 11am–3pm
Thermals are 255–327 ft/min from 11am to 3pm and peak at 327 ft/min at 1pm. The thermal top climbs to 2,440–2,760 ft above ground from noon to 2pm, and cloud base is well above it. Launch wind is 9–15 mph from 207–246°, within the preferred range; it swings to 269° by 4pm. Wind 3,000 ft above ground is 28–35 mph, so expect drift and stronger wind on climb-out. Air cools quickly with height (lapse rate 8.8 °C per km), which means sharp, punchy thermals: advanced pilots only.
West McClellan Marginal — Wind is mostly south-southwest, off this west-facing launch, and rises above 20 mph after 1pm, leaving only a brief noon window.
Window: 12pm–1pm
At noon, thermals reach 223 ft/min with a thermal top near 2,045 ft above ground, and wind is 12 mph from 232°, just south of the preferred 240–300°. From 1pm wind is 21–24 mph (peak 25 mph). Wind 3,000 ft above ground is 31–40 mph all day.
Daydreams Marginal — Wind lines up with launch and thermals are usable midday, but shear is in the hazardous range and wind builds through the afternoon.
Window: 11am–2pm
Thermals are 214–246 ft/min with a thermal top of about 1,470–2,219 ft above ground. Wind is 12–17 mph from 221–249°, within the preferred range, and ridge lift is about 240–350 ft/min. Wind rises to 20–23 mph by 3–4pm, so late-day and evening soaring is not advised. Peak shear is 12 mph per 100 m at 1,088 ft above ground, above the hazardous threshold.
Kingsbury grade Unfavorable — Wind is from the west-southwest all day, behind this southeast-facing launch, and turns very strong aloft after noon.
Peak thermal strength (w*) is only 206 feet per minute (ft/min) at 11am, with a thermal top (PBLH) of about 2,285 ft above ground (AGL) at noon. Surface wind is 226–271° all day, never near the preferred 104°, and reaches 24–31 mph by 2–3pm. Wind 1,000 ft above ground rises to 34–51 mph from 1pm.
Hallelujah Unfavorable — Wind is too strong and blows from the south, across this west/southwest launch, through the thermal hours.
Thermals peak at 283 ft/min at 1pm with a thermal top near 1,962 ft above ground. Launch wind is 23–26 mph from 187–204° from 10am to 1pm, outside the preferred 225–315° range. It eases to 8 mph at 3pm but stays from the south (184°). Shear is in the caution range (9 mph per 100 m at 571 ft above ground).
Slide Mountain Unfavorable — Strong tailwind of 25–37 mph and heavy sink on this south/southeast launch, with no usable thermals.
Wind is from 235–246° all day, building from 25 mph at 8am to 37 mph at 2pm. Wind 1,000 ft above ground reaches 50–54 mph from noon. Modeled ridge flow is sinking at 766 to 1,143 ft/min on the launch side. Thermals are essentially absent (peak 21 ft/min) in stable air.
Peavine Mountain Unfavorable — Launch wind of 24–32 mph all day, with 36–47 mph just above launch, is far too strong.
Direction (198–218°) suits the launch, but speeds are 28–32 mph from 10am onward. Thermals peak at 225 ft/min at 11am with a thermal top near 1,727 ft above ground. The model shows sinking ridge flow on the launch face all day.
Rainbow Ridge Unfavorable — Wind is from the southwest and west all day, behind this east/northeast launch.
Thermals are good (peak 331 ft/min at noon, thermal top about 2,400 ft above ground), but surface wind is 13–15 mph from 211–246° from 10am on, opposite the preferred 67°. Shear reaches the hazardous threshold (10 mph per 100 m at 1,488 ft above ground).
Duck Hill Unfavorable — Wind is never in the launch's west-to-north range: south-southeast in the morning, southwest and building in the afternoon.
Thermals peak at 301 ft/min at 1pm with a thermal top near 2,096 ft above ground. Morning wind is from 148–165°. Afternoon wind is from 224–242°, south of the preferred 270–50° range, and rises to 19–22 mph by 3–4pm. Evening conditions are not suitable either: late-day wind is cross and strengthening.

Hazards

  • Strong winds aloft and at high launches: Wind 1,000 ft above the high launches reaches 50–54 mph at Slide Mountain and 36–47 mph at Peavine, and the strongest site wind is 37 mph. Even at the lower sites, wind 3,000 ft above ground is 28–40 mph, so climbing out of the sheltered launches puts you into much stronger drift.
  • Low-level wind shear: The model shows hazardous shear at Daydreams (12 mph per 100 m) and Rainbow Ridge (10 mph per 100 m), and caution-level shear at Hallelujah (9 mph per 100 m). NWS Reno also expects increasing ridge winds Sunday with low-level wind shear (LLWS) and ridge gusts to 50 mph, no hourly timing given.
  • Possible lee-side turbulence and rotor: Flow at the Sierra crest (700 hPa, about crest height) over Reno is 24–30 knots from 211–223° from 8am to noon, mostly just south of the west-southwest direction that most reliably brings lee rotor. It then drops to 3–19 knots from 2pm to 4pm. The lee risk is unclear, but treat the air downwind of Peavine and the Carson Range as potentially rough, especially in late morning.
  • Sharp thermals: At McClellan, air cools quickly with height (8.8 °C per km), and thermal turbulence (sigma-w) reaches 1.1 m/s. Expect punchy, sharp-edged climbs from late morning to mid-afternoon; advanced pilots only.
  • Model confidence on ridge wind: At the Slide Mountain summit station, the model forecast a 41 mph mean wind against 26 mph observed, but observed gusts reached 52 mph. Valley airports also showed some misses: Reno-Stead was 4 mph stronger than forecast, and Minden direction was off by about 90°. Treat the exact ridge-level speeds with caution and expect gusts well above the hourly means.
  • Storm arriving Sunday night: NWS Reno expects a fast-moving storm late Sunday night with 50–65 mph ridge gusts and snow levels around 7,000–8,000 ft. This is after the flying day, but the model already shows wind building at most sites through the afternoon, so finish flying early.
